title: Staff and permissions
summary: Adding staff, what the roles control, and why the first user is different from everyone else.
html:
Staff are people in your business who log in. They are a different thing from customer contacts, who log into the portal and see only their own records.

Adding a staff member

Settings → Users, create the user, give them a login and assign a role. They get an email with their details if mail is working.

Roles

A role is a set of permissions. Permissions are per feature and per action — view, edit, create, delete — so a role can be allowed to see invoices but not edit them, or to create jobs but not delete anyone else's.

Build roles around what people do rather than around seniority. "Can raise an invoice but not credit one" is a sentence that maps onto a permission; "senior" is not.

The first user is special

The user created during installation is the super administrator, and some things are only ever available to it. If you are locked out of a setting, check whether you are logged in as that account.

Make sure it has a real email address on it and a password you have not reused. It is the account that can change everything.

Switching help on for everyone

A new installation shows the documentation to any staff member whose role allows it. If you want it restricted to the super administrator, tick Only show help menu for Super Administrator under Settings → Help.

On installations upgraded from an earlier version that restriction is already on, because it used to be the default. Untick it to let your staff read the documentation for the screen they are on.

When somebody leaves

Disable the login rather than deleting the user. Deleting removes the person who did the work from the records of the work; disabling stops the login and keeps the history.
